norms.what: A stage skill is model-invocable so the orchestrator can start it, which also lets Claude invoke it on an unrelated task; the run-file guard makes that cost one skill load. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).
After compaction the orchestrator, the oldest skill of the run, is the first to be dropped; re-invoking it restores the run's standing rules. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Discovery rests on today's docs, not a table written months ago. WebFetch runs the page through a small model and returns its answer, which cannot support a verbatim passage; the docs serve raw Markdown at `<page>.md`, which `curl` reads. Offline, the recorded passages are the only docs left, and every finding says they were not re-verified. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).
Some doc pages exceed the Read tool's limit, which returns only a partial view; reading by heading keeps each read whole and the context small. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

The digest is what the auditors and the verifier read instead of the pages, so a run fetches and reads each page once; it names each change with its passage, which is what a finding must quote. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

One brief shared by every agent keeps them classifying alike; agents never see the session, and those that set `omitClaudeMd` do not load the project memory, so the facts they need arrive as quoted `file:line` text, never as a paraphrase that could be wrong. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N40` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N40` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Writing each batch's lines before reading the next keeps no finding dependent on context that compaction could drop, and lets a resume tell which batches are done. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N08` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N08` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Parallel auditors finish a large inventory sooner; they pin their own model and effort, and Claude Code refuses spawns above its concurrent limit, so they go in waves. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N40` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N40` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

The per-transition audits checked files against a closed pattern table, which acted as the boundary of the search: a capability evaluation measured 58% recall for the skill against 79% for a session given the doc links (#34). Judging against the docs finds what no table names, and requiring the passage behind each finding keeps the precision the table gave. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

The items a closed inventory missed in that evaluation — a price table, a guide index, a version floor — each carry a token the docs name; searching the whole root for those tokens reaches them without listing them in advance. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Model-dependent behaviour can sit in a file the map does not name but a listed file points to; following leads within an approved budget keeps discovery open and its cost bounded. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

A file pinned to a third model is outside the transition; judging it against the target's docs would produce findings about the wrong model. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N10` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N10` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Signal words also appear in prose about other things, which produced false findings in early runs. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N41` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N41` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

An instruction outdated before the source model is outside this transition's evidence; reporting it as residue, with no change, keeps the audit within what its sources support. The examples differ per transition, so they come from the knowledge file. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N11` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N11` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

An audit that proposes removing a safety rule or a measured-failure rule does harm, whatever the docs say about tone or wording. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N12` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N12` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Anthropic's `claude-api` skill migrates request code with the right syntax for each SDK and platform, so the audit hands API findings off rather than editing them. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N25` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N25` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

A frontmatter `description` routes the skill or agent; urgency there is legitimate and not an instruction to the model about how to work. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N26` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N26` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Confidence tells the user how much to trust each finding; a system card describes an evaluation, not a rule, so a finding resting on it alone is low and cited by page and section. A project that already decided for the target should see that decision respected, with where it says so. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N31` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N31` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

A skill listed under `skills:` is injected in full into the agent at startup, and a custom subagent loads the project memory unless `omitClaudeMd` is set, so an instruction stated there is not missing; a `disable-model-invocation` skill cannot be preloaded. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N58` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N58` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Some techniques written for the source stay recommended for the target, and some settings serve the target's own fallback; flagging them would propose removing what the docs keep. The list is per transition, so it comes from the knowledge file. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N61` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Open discovery must say what it did not read, or its silence reads as a clean result; the account also shows how the docs were read, so an offline run is never taken for a verified one. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).
